world: A cold northern keep in the last year of a long siege. The garrison is thin and the watch rotations are brutal.
locationDesc: A stretch of wall above the frozen moat. Braziers stand at intervals along it and the sentries walk their beat between them; the relief watch changes on a fixed rotation.
action: Well past midnight, I pull my cloak tighter and walk the line of the wall.
note: explicit 'past midnight' — the clearest possible stated night

world: A fishing settlement on a hard coast, where the boats go out before light and the whole village lives by the tide.
locationDesc: A shingle beach where the boats are hauled up. Lamps hang along the sea wall and the crews load by hand.
action: The sky over the water has only just begun to grey and the sun is not up yet. I find the boat I was told to look for and wait to be noticed.
note: pre-sunrise: 'dawn' is the target, 'night' is a defensible read of the same passage

world: A trade city built around a single enormous covered market, where every guild keeps a stall and nothing is bought without argument.
locationDesc: The central aisle of the covered market. Roof vents run the length of it and the guild stalls crowd both sides.
action: The sun stands directly over the roof vents and the crowd is at its thickest. I push into it and look for the spice row.
note: sun overhead + peak trading — midday, with morning as the near-miss

world: A quiet farming valley where the households are large and the meals are the only time everyone is in one room.
locationDesc: The kitchen of a working farmhouse. A long table fills most of it and lamps stand along the dresser.
action: Supper is on the table and the light through the west window has gone deep orange. I take the empty seat and reach for the bread.

world: A company town organized entirely around a foundry that never stops running.
locationDesc: The foundry floor. The crews work in shifts around the clock and the shift bell governs everything that happens here.
action: It is a few hours past noon, midway through the second shift. I check the pour schedule pinned by the door.
note: 'a few hours past noon' — the case with competing signals; the heat and the far-off bell pull toward evening

world: A teaching hospital in a city that has been quietly running out of everything for a decade.
locationDesc: A ward of twenty beds with a row of windows down one side. Staff hand over between shifts and the trays go out at set times.
action: Morning rounds have just begun and the night staff are handing over. I follow the consultant to the first bed and listen.
note: a genuine morning, so accuracy cannot be gamed by never answering the default

world: A river port where the customs house sets the rhythm of every working day.
locationDesc: A long shed where cargo is weighed and taxed. Carters queue out into the yard and the clerks work straight through.
action: It is two hours past noon. I join the back of the queue and try to see how far ahead the desk is.
note: sibling to `shift` without the competing signals — isolates the relative-to-noon phrasing itself

world: A monastery whose day is divided by bells and whose scriptorium is its only source of income.
locationDesc: A hall of sloped desks under high windows. The copyists work to the rhythm of the monastery's bells.
action: There are a good two hours yet before noon. I find the desk I have been assigned and look at what is waiting on it.
note: relative-to-noon in the other direction — a model anchoring on 'noon' alone lands on midday

world: A lighthouse station on a shipping lane, worked by two keepers on opposite watches.
locationDesc: The glazed chamber at the top of the tower. The lamp turns steadily and there is nothing beyond the glass but open water.
action: Some three hours past midnight, I check the oil reservoir and note the level in the book.
note: relative to midnight rather than noon — the small hours, where `night` must not drift to `evening`

world: A cavalry post on a frontier road, where patrols go out at the earliest usable light.
locationDesc: A gravel yard in front of the stables. Patrols form up here before riding out.
action: The light has been up perhaps an hour and the frost is still on the rails. I look for the sergeant and report myself ready.
note: relative to first light — dawn or early morning are both defensible, so both are accepted

action: I look around for whoever is closest and ask where the ferry puts in.
note: a lantern hangs here, but nothing says when — the ambient-light trap

action: I set my pack down and take stock of the room.
note: a lamp burns green; again ambience, not a time

action: I walk the length of the works, looking for anything out of place.
note: underground — the one setting where a daypart is arguably meaningless

action: I step off the path and listen for anything moving.
note: forest canopy: 'the sky is hidden, but plenty of light still reaches the floor'

action: I head across campus to find where I am supposed to be.
note: contemporary town, no time language at all
